When the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt MUST direct it to keep the requirement's full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.
rationale:
The subject sets two prompt obligations. The review prompt must direct the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question. When the reviewer splits a requirement, the prompt must direct it to keep the full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_never_renames_and_names_split_parts]` is marked `{test}`. It extracts the prompt's "Mechanical changes" section with `review_prompt_between`, which collapses whitespace and panics if either delimiter is missing. It then uses `assert_text` to require each of these phrases:
- "Never rename or move a committed requirement; if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question" covers the no-rename/no-move rule and the design-question redirect.
- "When you split one, keep its full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`" covers keeping the full name on the core obligation and the part-naming scheme.
- "List every new name" covers listing the new names.

`assert_text` asserts `contains` for every phrase, so removing any of these directives would fail the test. The subject's obligations apply to prompt content, and checking the text is the appropriate test for that. I found no obligation left untested.
